what: Phonics for Kids is a friendly set of reading activities for early readers learning English. Children learn letter sounds A–Z with a picture and word for each, blend three-letter words like c-a-t, meet letter teams such as sh, ch, ee and ai, practise sight words in four levels and play a picture sound game.

Words are spoken by your device's built-in English voice. Because computer voices are not reliable at single sounds, each sound is shown with a simple mouth-sound spelling such as /m/ – mmm, lips together, and the voice says carefully chosen example words slowly.
Stars and progress are saved in this browser only. It is for English only.
uses: Each letter with a picture, a word and how to say it.
Watch the sounds light up one by one and join into a word.
sh, ch, th, ck, ng, ee, oo, ai, oa, igh and more.
Four levels of common tricky words.
Which picture starts with this sound?
Tips on saying pure sounds and keeping it fun.
tutorial: Pick an English voice and a slow talking speed. If no voice is found, use the pictures and hints and say the sounds yourself.
Tap a letter, hear the example word and read the Say it hint together. Tap I know this sound for a star.
Open Blending, choose a vowel and press Blend it. Say each sound as it lights up, then the whole word.
Tap a team like sh and hear the example words, with the team shown in red.
Use Word cards to read, or Listen and find to hear a word and tap it.
Look at the letter and tap the picture that starts with its sound. Ten rounds, one star for each first try.
features: Picture, word, sound spelling and mouth hint for each.
50 three-letter words in five vowel groups.
Distractors never share the target's first sound.
Clear note and hints when the device has no English voice.
Made for small hands on phones and tablets.

example.title: Worked example: blending cat
example.text: Open Blending and choose the vowel a. The tiles c, a and t show /k/, /a/ and /t/. Press Blend it: each tile lights up while your child says the sound, then the tiles slide together, the cat picture appears and the voice says cat slowly and then normally. Tap I read it! to earn a star.

tips: Keep sessions short: 5 to 10 minutes a day.
Say pure sounds: mmm, not muh. Keep quick sounds like b, d, p and t short.
Use the Very slow speed for younger children.
Your own voice is the best model; play the word after you say the sound.
Turn off Fun sounds for a quiet room.
Use Show words under the pictures in the game for children who are starting to read.
problems: Check the device volume and silent switch. If the note says no English voice was found, add an English text-to-speech voice in your device settings and reload.
The voice sounds strange on single letters
That is why the tool speaks example words, not single sounds. Use the Say it hint for the sound itself.
Stars are saved in this browser. Private windows, clearing site data or another browser start fresh.
Pictures are emoji, so they look a little different on each phone or computer.
